items.title: AMD finalizes $8.2 billion World Labs acquisition, adds 'godmother of AI' as EVP and chief scientist
items.summary: AMD on Monday announced that it has finalized its acquisition of Fei-Fei Li's World Labs.

items.title: AMD, Broadcom stocks sink on tighter US chip rules, CoreWeave and Nebius shares drop
items.summary: Chip and AI infrastructure stocks moved lower as the US moved to restrict semiconductor exports to China in the wake of Nvidia's CEO scandal.

items.title: Why AMD Stock Was Sliding Today
items.summary: A new set of export restrictions on Southeast Asia poses a new threat to AMD and the chip sector.

items.title: ARM's 50% Licensing Revenue Surge Signals Strong AI-Driven Demand
items.summary: Arm Holdings' licensing revenues surge 50% to $773M in Q2 FY27, fueled by AI demand and advanced chip designs, while growing royalties bolster its outlook.

items.title: Jensen Huang Reportedly Considers Returning To Nvidia: FT
items.summary: Jensen Huang reportedly is mulling a return to the chip giant he founded, days after resigning as Nvidia CEO in scandal. Nvidia stock was indicated little changed.

items.title: AMD Completes World Labs Acquisition, Appoints Fei-Fei Li as Chief Scientist
items.summary: AMD (NASDAQ:AMD) announced the completion of its acquisition of World Labs, an artificial intelligence company specialising in models capable of generating and simulating interactive three-dimensional environments. The transaction expands AMD’s AI research capabilities and brings World Labs’ model development team into the semiconductor company’s operations.

items.title: U.S. chip stocks slide as traders unwind Nvidia rival bets before earnings
items.summary: Investing.com -- U.S. chip stocks are down sharply on Monday as traders took profits on recent gains in Nvidia’s rivals ahead of the AI giant’s earnings, while worries about tighter export controls added to the pressure.

items.title: AI Chip Stocks Extend Their Sell-Off as Monday Opens Deep in the Red
items.summary: Chip stocks face a ~$260B hit at Monday's open after losing $650B in two days, as Nvidia's CEO crisis, rising yields and export fears.
